notes.text: Ibn Sina, commonly known in the West as Avicenna, was a preeminent philosopher and physician of the Muslim world.
Avicenna was a seminal figure of the Islamic Golden Age, serving in the courts of various Iranian rulers, and was influential to medieval European medical and Scholastic thought.
Avicenna is remembered as a philosopher connected with Uzbekistan.
Avicenna's recorded life dates place this profile around 980-1037.
Avicenna is grouped with Philosophy, Ethics & Religion in the People Library.
